page: Microsoft Azure E96-24s_v5 is an ESv5-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The server is configured with 24 virtual CPUs derived from 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 28.0 GB per vCPU. The CPU cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 105 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include any GPUs or local storage, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate average to strong performance characteristics. The server demonstrates strong memory performance, with a PassMark memory score of 2894.78 and a large-block write memory bandwidth of 106.74 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, fall within the average range, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 12123.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 23302.98. For specialized tasks, the instance achieves a strong text generation speed of 263.29 tokens/sec during LLM inference with a small 135M model, while maintaining average throughput for larger models and static web serving.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E96-24s_v5 offers high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a specialized choice for memory-bound workloads rather than compute-heavy tasks. The lack of local storage means all storage operations must rely on external Premium Storage, which represents a key architectural tradeoff. Given its massive 672.0 GB memory capacity and strong memory write bandwidth, this server is highly suited for large in-memory databases, caching layers such as Redis, enterprise applications with high memory footprints, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
